\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Junta}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.KKL.Junta
\section{Overview}
Influential coordinates capture low degree Fourier mass and give Boolean approximations under a Fourier tail bound. Choosing the degree cutoff yields the dimension-independent Friedgut junta theorem.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier mass on influential coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowInfluence_fourierConcentration}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.exists_boolean_junta_of_fourier_omission, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourier_omission_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.disagreementProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords, KKL.influential_coords_card}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, and $k\in\mathbb N$. Write $I=I(f)$, put $\tau=1$ if $I=0$ and $\tau=\varepsilon^2/(I^2 9^k)$ otherwise, and set $J=\{i:I_i(f)\ge\tau\}$. Then $|J|\le I^3 9^k/\varepsilon^2$ and $\sum_{|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}\widehat f(S)^2\le\varepsilon$; if $\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat f(S)^2\le\varepsilon$, then $\sum_{\neg(S\subseteq J\ \mathrm{and}\ |S|\le k)}\widehat f(S)^2\le2\varepsilon$ and there exists $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ with $\Pr(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Friedgut exponential junta theorem]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.friedgut_junta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourierWeightAbove_le_totalInfluence_div_succ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowInfluence_fourierConcentration, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords}
\difficulty{5}
There exists an absolute $C>0$ such that for every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ under the uniform law and $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ with $|J|\le\exp(CI(f)/\varepsilon)$, $\sum_{\neg(S\subseteq J\ \mathrm{and}\ |S|\le I(f)/\varepsilon)}\widehat f(S)^2\le2\varepsilon$, and $\Pr(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Optimized junta from a Fourier tail]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.optimized_junta_of_fourier_tail}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.exists_boolean_junta_of_fourier_omission, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.fourier_omission_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.disagreementProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords, KKL.influential_coords_card}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube with $I=I(f)>0$. For $\varepsilon,\eta>0$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ satisfying $\sum_{|S|>k}\widehat f(S)^2\le\varepsilon$, put $\rho=\eta/(2+\eta)$. There exist $J\subseteq[n]$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$, with $|J|\le I^{2+\eta}/(\varepsilon\rho^k)^{1+\eta}$ and $\Pr(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
\end{lemma}
